title: From broadcasting to platforms
paragraphs: Before the contemporary dominance of streaming and social networks, television broadcasting, recorded media, regional distribution, and fan communities provided important routes for Korean entertainment beyond national borders. Different parts of Asia became significant spaces of circulation and reception, with particular programs and performers gaining traction through channels that changed over time.

Digital networks later transformed speed and scale. A performance could circulate through videos, excerpts, shared commentary, and user-created materials. Streaming platforms enabled some audiences to discover Korean-language content without first encountering it through domestic television schedules or traditional import channels.

This transformation produced new kinds of intermediaries. Translators, online communities, recommendation systems, critics, influencers, and independent fans could all affect visibility. Technology supplied channels, but actual cultural attachment came from people choosing to listen, watch, discuss, and return.
